destination.name: Huzhou
destination.tagline: A Taihu-shore prefecture city of silk, brush-making and Nanxun canal town gardens
destination.description: Huzhou lies on the south shore of Lake Tai, a prefecture city long tied to silk and to the Huzhou brush, a craft known since the Jin dynasty. The city holds a free museum, the restored Yuan-dynasty garden of Lianhuazhuang and a brush museum with live demonstrations. Nanxun, a canal town of Ming and Qing bridges, merchant mansions and a private library, is the main canal-town draw, and Anji's bamboo hills lie to the south-west in the same prefecture.
whyVisit: Wander a canal town of merchant mansions

goodToKnow.title: Start with the museums
goodToKnow.detail: Huzhou Museum is free to enter, and the Brush Museum runs live brush-making demonstrations.

goodToKnow.title: Anji is in the prefecture
goodToKnow.detail: Anji, with its bamboo hills, lies south-west of the city in Huzhou prefecture and has its own sights.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Mild, clear weather in {months} suits canal walks. Summers are sticky, with June rains.

notes: Anji mention kept but corrected to 'south-west, same prefecture' (Anji coordinates 30.56,119.65 vs Huzhou 30.86,120.10). Cut: 'best-known day trip', 'quiet base', side trip from Hangzhou/Shanghai, Nanxun-free tip (only a weak Ctrip note). Unverified: bestMonths/blurb.
